newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees inflation at 6.3 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: China sees inflation at 6.3 pct in 1997.

text.p: A top Chinese research group has forecast inflation of about 6.3 percent and economic growth of 10.5 percent in 1997, the Financial News said on Thursday.
The State Information Centre was making the prediction in a recent report, according to the newspaper.
China's central bank governor Dai Xianglong has said inflation this year would be below 6.6 percent and economic growth would be nine to 10 percent.

The report based its forecast on expectations of a continuation of "appropriately tight" monetary policies by the central bank next year coupled with a favourable domestic and international economic climate.
The report also forecast a trade surplus of $15.9 billion next year compared with an expected surplus of $10 billion this year. It put exports at $171.2 billion and imports at $155.3 billion in 1997.
The report also put industrial output growth at 15.2 percent in 1997, up 2.1 percentage points from the expected level for 1996.

Fixed asset investment in 1997 would reach 2.823 trillion yuan ($340 billion), up 18.5 percent from the expected 1996 level. Retail sales are expected to reach 2.934 trillion yuan, up 19.7 percent, the report said.
